messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.patel@globex-corp.com>, Anita Chen <anita.chen@globex-corp.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Jul 2028 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Identity cutover: observability & IP allowlist plan

Hi Raj / Anita —

Thanks again for locking the July 28 cutover window. Per our call today, attaching the checklist, canary plan, and the SAML metadata export. This thread will track the identity-focused runbook items that need sign-off prior to cutover. High-level asks:

- Confirm the IP ranges for your egress/load balancer that we should add to Redwood's allowlist (below).
- Confirm the SCIM mapping for the service-account group (scim:service_accounts -> Redwood role mapping).
- Provide an estimated user migration batch size for the first canary (we suggested 20 users).

Key dates:
- Cutover (production): Thu Jul 28, 2028 22:00-23:30 PDT (maintenance window)
- Canary rollout: first 60 minutes of the window (20 users)
- Full sync: after canary success, phased 1h/1000 users pace

Pre-cutover telemetry we will enable:
- SAML assertion latency and failure rate (alert if >3% failures in 5m)
- SCIM provisioning errors by user and attribute (alert on 1st critical failure)
- Authn success rate and average latency by region
- Service account token issuance and rotation events

Attached: cutover checklist.xlsx, canary-plan.pdf, saml-metadata.xml

Action owners (please reply in-thread with confirmations):
- Globex: provide IP ranges, confirm SCIM mapping, confirm canary list (Raj / Anita)
- Redwood (me + Neha): finalize RBAC mapping and audit events, wire up telemetry dashboards (Jonas)

Notes on rollback criteria (draft):
- Any SAML failure spike above 5% for 10m -> automatic rollback to previous SAML issuer config
- Any SCIM provisioning that results in >0 critical failures (account disabled) for 5 users -> pause and investigate

Thanks — not a long list but timing is tight.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Sr. Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0198

Thanks Grace — quick clarifying Qs before we sign off: 

1) IP ranges: our outbound egress will come from the NAT pool below (please add to allowlist):
- 34.198.12.0/22
- 34.198.16.0/21

2) SCIM: We're OK with the mapping you proposed but need the exact attribute names. Our SCIM uses 'externalId' for legacy ids; can you map that to 'redwood_user_id' rather than overwriting 'id'?

3) Service accounts: we have two long-lived service accounts that will be used by our automation runner. They will authenticate with SAML-to-service-account exchange; will Redwood issue long-lived API keys or short-lived tokens? We prefer short-lived tokens (15m) with automated rotation.

4) Telemetry: can you give a sample of the dashboard events/fields? We need to align with our SIEM ingestion.

Also — can we move the start time 30 minutes earlier (21:30 PDT) to reduce overlap with our internal batch jobs? If so we need to confirm with your on-call.

--

Raj — thanks, good questions. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) IP ranges: our outbound egress will come from the NAT pool below (please add to allowlist):
> - 34.198.12.0/22
> - 34.198.16.0/21

Confirmed — we've started the request with infra. Please expect a confirmation ticket by EOD.

> 2) SCIM: We're OK with the mapping you proposed but need the exact attribute names. Our SCIM uses 'externalId' for legacy ids; can you map that to 'redwood_user_id' rather than overwriting 'id'?

Yes — Neha will attach the exact CSV mapping. We will map externalId -> redwood_user_id and preserve scim:id. No overwrites.

> 3) Service accounts: ... will Redwood issue long-lived API keys or short-lived tokens?

Redwood issues short-lived tokens by default. For automation runners we can support a client-credential flow that mints 15-minute tokens and writes rotation events to audit logs. Jonas will confirm the rotation cadence and the endpoint.

> 4) Telemetry: can you give a sample of the dashboard events/fields?

Attaching a quick event sample and the dashboard link in the runbook. Fields include: event_type, user_id/redwood_user_id, assertion_id, saml_error_code, scim_error_code, latency_ms, region, service_account_id. We also publish a webhook for aggregated alerts (SIEM-friendly).

> Also — can we move the start time 30 minutes earlier (21:30 PDT) to reduce overlap with our internal batch jobs?

We can accommodate 21:30 PDT start. Changing window to 21:30-23:00 PDT. Please confirm final approval so we can notify on-call and Ops.

I'll circulate the updated checklist with these specifics shortly.

— Grace

On a related note: internal owners, please see the action items I assigned in the checklist. Jonas — can you confirm the alert thresholds and the webhook payload example? Neha — please share the CSV mapping and the SCIM attribute validation rules.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Identity cutover: observability & IP allowlist plan

All — attaching the updated cutover-checklist (v1.2) and the canary plan PDF with concrete pass/fail gates. Summary of the SCIM mapping and service-account guidance below: 

SCIM mapping (CSV fields):
- scim:id -> scim_id (preserve)
- externalId -> redwood_user_id (map)
- userName -> username
- name.givenName -> first_name
- name.familyName -> last_name
- emails[type=work].value -> email

Validation rules we will enforce during the sync (canary will run these):
- email must be RFC 5322 valid; invalid addresses get flagged but not created (manual review)
- redwood_user_id cannot collide with existing accounts; collisions will pause the import and surface to the CS team

Service accounts:
- We will issue short-lived tokens (15m) for service accounts by default. For your automation runner we recommend using the client-credentials path with certificate-based auth (mTLS).
- Rotation: tokens rotate every 10 minutes; we surface a rotation event to audit-logs with service_account_id and key_id. We can support a 1-hour grace window if your runner cannot handle 15m tokens — note this increases blast radius.

Canary gates (excerpt):
- Authentication: 0.5% max failure rate over 15m for canary users
- Provisioning: zero critical SCIM failures (disabled accounts, role mismatches) for canary batch
- Telemetry: SIEM webhook delivered and acknowledged by Globex endpoint for aggregated alert test

Rollback steps (condensed):
1) Pause provisioning and flip SAML issuer to previous metadata (automated rollback job)
2) Revoke recently issued service tokens and re-open support channel
3) Run account integrity checks and re-run safe sync

Next actions:
- Raj: reply with final canary user list and confirm SIEM webhook URL (we'll send a test)
- Jonas: publish the sample webhook payload and set alert thresholds in NewRelic/Datadog dashboards
- Marissa: schedule the post-cutover audit and confirm retention policy for the audit logs (Globex requirement: 13 months)

Thanks — I'll also post the checklist to the Jira ticket.
